The group's leading regional franchise, extensive distribution network capabilities as one of Singapore’s largest retail brokerages position it to capture structural growth in trading activity driven by Singapore's equity market reforms, while scaling higher-quality recurring wealth management fee income.
This diversification should improve earnings visibility, enhance return on equity and support a structural re-rating over time. Today, wealth segment contributes approx. one-third of its total revenues.

Revenues grew strongly at >15% CAGR since 2022, primarily led by a similar c.15% CAGR in commission income and c.40% CAGR in trading income.
Momentum of higher trading activities in Singapore and Hong Kong has accelerated into FY26F, with SGX SDAV growing at c.46% y/y during 5MCY26, and HKEX seeing c.14% y/y growth.
We continue to expect commission income and trading income to grow at similar trajectory in FY25A, ~29% and 34% y/y respectively in FY26F, penciling in a ~15% total revenue growth in FY26F and 13% total revenue growth in FY27F.

UOBKH also has high positive correlation to SGX’s securities traded values (>0.8), and is a strong proxy to the Singapore equities market.

title: Wang Yi says China welcomes stronger European business relations
article:
(July 5): China welcomes deeper cooperation with Swedish and European businesses, which will benefit all parties involved, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said in a meeting with Investor AB chairman Jacob Wallenberg in Stockholm on July 4, according to a statement from the ministry on Sunday.

Wang said the Wallenbergs were among the first of the European groups to enter the Chinese market after the nation’s reform and opening-up, and the Swedish firm had made a unique contribution to relations between the two countries.

The minister said he looked to the Wallenberg family and Sweden’s business community to continue playing a positive role in supporting improved ties between the two countries. China and Sweden are working to improve mutual trust, focus on cooperation and return bilateral relations to a healthy development track, he said.

Wang said China would continue to boost domestic demand, advance opening-up at a high level, and uphold free-trade and market economy principles.

title: NZ pledges trade talks with Brazil, Europe within five years
article:
(July 5): New Zealand’s governing National Party will begin negotiations for seven new trade deals within five years should it win the November election, Trade Minister Todd McClay said.

Talks with Brazil, Switzerland, Argentina, Bangladesh, Nigeria, Uruguay and the European Free Trade Association bloc would be prioritised in that five-year period, McClay said in an emailed statement Sunday. The seven markets currently account for just NZ$1.8 billion (US$1 billion) worth of the nation’s exports and offer “huge, untapped opportunities,” McClay said.

Focus would then shift to negotiations with countries including South Africa, Türkiye and Sri Lanka over the next decade, he said.

The trade push follows an uptick of deals signed during the government’s term including a pact with India in April that is tipped to deliver a surge in primary exports in coming years. NZ also completed an agreement with the European Union in 2024. Data last month showed the EU has overtaken Australia as New Zealand’s third-biggest market for primary exports.

The latest announcement comes ahead of a national election to be held on Nov 7. Support for the National Party, which governs in a coalition, fell to its lowest level since 2021 in a key opinion poll last month.

title: Investors looking for shelter from AI storm are turning to India
article:
(July 5): After losing out big on the global AI rally, Indian equities are regaining the attention of investors seeking to weather the latest market turbulence.

With the artificial intelligence (AI) frenzy roiling benchmark gauges from Asia to the US, the NSE Nifty 50 Index is becoming a safe haven of sorts for global investors. In the first half of the year, it moved 1% or more on just about one-third of the days — less than the MSCI Emerging Markets Index and barely more than the S&P 500 Index.

India’s lack of AI plays has been a hurdle most of the year as investors turned to markets like South Korea and Taiwan that delivered stellar returns. But with concerns mounting over the sustainability of that trade, interest in India is slowly coming back. In June, the Nifty 50 outperformed the MSCI Emerging Markets Index by the most since November, while foreign outflows were the smallest in four months.

“India’s calm comes down to one thing: It sits outside the AI trade,” said Maxence Visseau, chief investment officer of Arkevium Capital in Dubai. His firm is neutral on the market and uses it as a diversifier, he said. “India works as an AI hedge inside the EM complex.”

Indian equities remain some of the world’s worst performers this year, but the tide is starting to turn as the rupee stabilises after hitting a record low and oil gains that tanked shares of refiners and airlines recede on easing tensions in the Middle East. That has reduced inflation concerns and brightened prospects for India’s economic growth, according to a government report at the end of June.

See also: Australia to sign Fiji security pact, finalise India uranium export deal, newspaper says

At the same time, market players are getting more upbeat about the upcoming earnings season, which Tata Consultancy Services Ltd kicks off on Thursday.

“The fall in commodity prices has altered the macro outlook for India almost overnight,” said Sandip Sabharwal, founder of research house Asksandipsabharwal.com in Mumbai. “Lower commodity prices, improving capital flows and stable interest rates create an environment where earnings upgrades are likely to exceed downgrades over the coming quarters.”

See also: Justice Department defends move to drop Adani criminal charges

In a note to clients, Morgan Stanley analysts including Ridham Desai wrote last month that India has become a “much larger macro asset class.” The less volatile inflation data in recent years support equity valuations and turn the market into one of defensive growth that can withstand global shocks better than it used to, they said. Over the past decade, the Nifty 50 almost tripled, delivering annual gains of more than 10% on six separate years.

The benchmark index logged 38 sessions with moves of 1% or more in either direction in the first six months of 2026, compared with 59 for MSCI’s emerging-market and Asian gauges and 32 for the S&P 500. South Korea’s Kospi index was off the charts, with 79 days of fluctuations of at least 1% — or two-thirds of the days in 2026.

Meanwhile, the India NSE Volatility Index dropped for a third straight month in June, falling below its one-year average and reaching its lowest level since February on Friday. That’s a far cry from April, when the gauge of option prices was at a one-year high relative to the Cboe Volatility Index, shortly after the Nifty 50 tanked to a low.

Kruti Shah, a quantitative analyst at Equirus Securities, sees a “bullish undertone” in the Nifty 50 and favorus call spreads to bet on more gains, adding that the upcoming earnings season may offer some positive surprises.

“India was held back earlier this year by higher energy prices, elevated valuations and limited exposure to the AI trade,” said Ben Powell, chief investment strategist for the Middle East and Asia Pacific at BlackRock Investment Institute. “As those pressures have eased, investors may look beyond AI-heavy markets. That could put India back on investors’ radar as a differentiated opportunity within emerging markets.”

title: Australia to sign Fiji security pact, finalise India uranium export deal, newspaper says
article:
(July 5): Australia is poised to sign a new security agreement with Fiji and finalise a deal to export uranium to India during a series of meetings this week, The Australian newspaper reported.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will travel to Fiji on Monday to sign the “Vuvale Union” with his Fijian counterpart, the newspaper reported Saturday, without citing sources. The pact may approach the level of the mutual-defence treaty with Papua New Guinea that is set to come into effect this week, the newspaper said.

Australia is stepping up its diplomatic efforts in the Pacific, adding to security and policing deals with Papua New Guinea, Tuvalu, Nauru, Indonesia and others in a bid to contain Chinese influence in the region. The treaty with Fiji builds on an earlier partnership signed in 2019. The two sides reached a basic agreement in May, pending the finalisation of details.

Albanese is set to reach a deal to export uranium to India during a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Melbourne later in the week, The Australian also reported. The two sides have resolved technical issues around non-proliferation safeguards, paving the way for an agreement, it said, citing sources it didn’t identify.

title: Justice Department defends move to drop Adani criminal charges
article:
(July 5): The US Justice Department defended its move to drop the criminal case against Gautam Adani, arguing that securities charges against the Indian billionaire never should have been brought in the first place.

R Trent McCotter, principal associate deputy attorney general, said in a filing to a US judge on Saturday that the department’s move in May to abandon the case wasn’t “a close call.” The Brooklyn-based federal judge overseeing the case, Nicholas G Garaufis, asked the department last month to explain its decision to ditch the blockbuster case filed in 2024 at the end of the Biden administration.

The indictment, which accused Adani and others of a scheme to pay more than US$250 million in bribes to Indian government officials to lock in solar energy contracts, immediately drew some criticism as an .overreach The Justice Department claimed some of the accused, including Adani, had lied about the alleged scheme when seeking to raise capital from US and international investors.

In May, the Justice Department said it had decided “not to devote further resources to these criminal charges.” Garaufis had given the department a deadline of later this month to explain its reasoning.

Among the explanations McCotter presented for dropping the case were that it was a foreign matter and would have presented “extraordinary proof problems.” He also argued that “not a single penny has ever been lost on the securities at issue.”

“The United States pretending to be the world police can cause diplomatic strife and also wastes resources better spent on domestic concerns,” McCotter said. “India can better manage its internal systems than can prosecutors in Brooklyn and Washington.”

See also: StanChart targets mid-sized African companies for debt sales

He added that India has “investigated many of the allegations in this case and in several reports and decisions issued in 2026 has found no actionable misconduct.”

An Adani Group representative had no immediate comment. A lawyer for Gautam Adani declined to comment.

McCotter also told Garaufis that the department’s discretion to dismiss cases is protected by the US Constitution. He said that it would be “problematic to hold defendants’ dismissals hostage while the Court questions an outcome all parties have agreed is appropriate.”

See also: India, Japan sign over 100 deals from mushrooms to the moon

He said the decision to move to drop the case was entirely based on a review of the merits of the matter and denied that a pledge by Adani to invest in the US played any role in the decision.

The billionaire had publicly said he planned to invest US$10 billion just after Americans elected Trump as president in late 2024. Among more than 100 slides that Adani’s legal team used to argue against the criminal case this year was one that referenced the US$10 billion pledge, Bloomberg has reported.

“The Department should be credited for ending these criminal security charges before having to endure a likely loss on the merits,” McCotter wrote.

“I was the final and sole decision maker to seek dismissal of the charges here,” he also said elsewhere in the filing.
